questions.text: What would motivate you to use the vim editor for configuration files rather than vi? (2)
questions.correctAnswer: Vim adds syntax highlighting, which makes different parts of a configuration file easier to recognise and can help reveal typing mistakes. It also offers editing improvements such as multiple undo levels, completion and better search support. Syntax highlighting does not prove that a configuration is valid.

Gives another valid Vim improvement or clearly explains the benefit of spotting configuration mistakes more easily (1).
Do not require or reward the claim that Vim fully validates every configuration file.

questions.explanation:
Vim is an extended vi editor. Its extra features can make configuration files easier to read and edit.

Why: Syntax highlighting separates comments, keywords and values visually, making mistakes easier to notice. Features such as multiple undo levels make correcting an edit easier. These are concrete improvements over traditional vi.

Student note: Give a feature and its benefit. For example: syntax highlighting helps me spot a misspelled setting.

study.title: Vim for configuration files
study.simple: Vim is an extended vi editor. Its extra features can make configuration files easier to read and edit.
whyCorrect: Syntax highlighting separates comments, keywords and values visually, making mistakes easier to notice. Features such as multiple undo levels make correcting an edit easier. These are concrete improvements over traditional vi.
notes: Configuration files control how a service behaves.
Syntax highlighting helps you read the structure of a file.
Use the service's own validation command to check whether the saved configuration is actually valid.
steps: Configuration files control how a service behaves.

study.example: In Vim, :syntax on enables highlighting when the file type and installed syntax support are available.
study.pitfall: Colouring is a reading aid, not a complete configuration test.
